reading.text:
# Reading: def WellPosedness.System.PredForcing.mk (constructor)

The constructor's arguments must be: an underlying forcing (five components with their
progressive measurability and square-integrability) and the predictability of the jump component
q^h (P (x) E-measurable / predictable L^2(nu)-valued). Faithful iff the argument list yields
exactly the paper's class of square-integrable forcings with predictable q^h.

comparison.text:
# Comparison: def System.PredForcing.mk (constructor)

PredForcing.mk takes exactly (1) a Forcing F P nu T q (the five components with their
measurability, vanishing and square-integrability fields) and (2) qh_pred: each coordinate of
q^h marked predictable. These are the fields of PredForcing; nothing else. Same representation
choices as PredForcing (extension by 0, the library's marked predictable sigma-algebra, which fixes
the null time 0).
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices, each harmless:
1. Built as Forcing (coordinates, extension by 0 off [0,T], progressive q^b, q^sigma, q^f,
   finite energies, q^g_T in L^2(F_T)) plus marked predictability of q^h.
2. Marked predictability is for the sigma-algebra generated by F x (r,q] x B with r >= 0,
   F in F_r, nu(B) < oo: for sigma-finite nu this is P (x) E on positive times, and it forces
   q^h(0) = 0 for a q^h vanishing before 0, whereas the paper's P (x) E allows a nonzero F_0 x E
   measurable value at time 0; time 0 is Lebesgue-null and does not enter (4.1), so the classes
   agree up to that null modification.
